title: RayCast
subtitle: Your media, organised. On any screen.
summary: A local media hub: organise your library, then cast it, a browser tab, or your whole screen to the TV, with your phone as the remote.
description: RayCast runs as a local web app on your computer. It organises your videos into shows and movies with artwork, remembers where you left off, and casts to a Chromecast or, experimentally, another browser. It can also cast a browser tab or your whole screen, and a phone companion puts the remote in your pocket. Your media stays on your own network.
features: A library that organises itself
Scan a folder, preview the changes, then sort everything into show and season folders, with undo.
Three ways to cast
Local videos, a browser tab through the extension, or your whole screen, to any Chromecast.
Any browser, a new screen
Pair another computer or tablet and use it as a cast screen (experimental).
Your phone, the remote
Scan a QR code to browse, cast, and control playback. No app store, no account.
Subtitles that fit
Choose tracks, nudge the timing, import downloads, and repair out-of-sync subtitles locally.
Playback that recovers
Checks compatibility, converts when needed, retries on failure, and resumes where you left off.

title: Edgewise
subtitle: Where the markets disagree.
summary: An on-demand research tool that lines up prediction-market odds across exchanges and shows where they don’t agree.
description: The same question can carry different odds on different prediction markets. Edgewise puts those prices side by side, highlights meaningful gaps, and explains every signal it raises. It only runs when you ask, keeps its data on your own machine, and never places a trade. It’s a research tool, not a trading bot.
features: Odds, side by side
One row per prediction, with each exchange’s price next to the others.
Signals that explain themselves
Every flag shows its prices, volume, and exactly why it qualified.
Only when you ask
No background scanning. Every query is bounded, cancellable, and timestamped.
Test it on paper
A virtual portfolio follows signals without real money or real orders.

title: World Cup 2026
subtitle: The whole tournament. In one place.
summary: A self-running tournament tracker that follows all 104 matches live, from the first kickoff to the final whistle.
description: World Cup 2026 follows every match on its own. It collects live scores every 30 seconds, cross-checks them against a second source, and pushes updates to every open screen within seconds. Group standings, the knockout bracket, and detailed match threads update themselves, and the whole tournament exports as a printable A3 wall chart.
features: Runs itself
Live scores for all 104 matches, collected every 30 seconds and cross-checked for accuracy.
A bracket that fills itself in
Winners advance automatically, using FIFA tiebreakers and the best third-place rules.
Every match, closer
Event timelines, stats, momentum, win probability, and lineups.
Live on every screen
Updates arrive within seconds, with alerts for goals, red cards, and results.
On paper, too
Printable A3 wall charts and bracket posters, generated as PDFs.
Ready for match day
A simulation mode for testing, and an alert when the data source needs attention.
